record.idea: An AI vision system that, using a smartphone camera, analyzes raw potato slices (shape, thickness, starch content approximation via translucency) and suggests optimal oil temperature and cooking time *before* frying.
record.gap: Cooks struggle to consistently prepare raw potatoes for optimal frying, leading to guesswork about oil temperature and cooking time.
record.removed_assumption: Assumes a cook can accurately judge raw potato characteristics and translate them into optimal cooking parameters.
record.who_has_problem: Home cooks and professional chefs who aim for consistent tortilla quality. "Potato preparation: Potatoes should be cut into thin slices (around 1/8 inch thick) to cook thoroughly. A major mistake is not cooking the potatoes properly; they need to be confited gently at around 130°C, rather than seared, to ensure they are soft inside without being raw. Using too little oil during this stage is a common error, as potatoes need to be cooked in abundant oil to confit and fry correctly." (https://tortilladepatatas.org/en/guides/classic-tortilla-masterclass/)
record.why_now: Advances in AI vision combined with smartphone camera capabilities allow for real-time analysis of food properties and complex parameter estimation.
record.buildable: Yes, AI vision for object recognition (shape, thickness) is mature. Starch approximation via translucency would require specific research and data but is plausible with current AI capabilities and specialized imaging techniques.

record.idea: A haptic feedback system for the "flip". It uses a weighted pan simulator and force sensors to teach the precise wrist flick required, with AI analyzing the force curve and giving real-time corrective feedback.
record.gap: Many aspiring tortilla makers find the crucial pan flip too challenging to master consistently, often resulting in failed attempts.
record.removed_assumption: Assumes that mastering the tortilla flip is primarily about intuitive feel rather than learnable, precise mechanics.
record.who_has_problem: Aspiring home cooks and culinary students struggling with the delicate "physics of the flip". "The 'physics of the flip' is a critical technique" (https://magefesausa.com/how-to-prepare-the-perfect-spanish-omelette/)
record.why_now: Maturation of haptic feedback technologies, advanced force sensors, and AI-driven movement analysis (e.g., in sports or rehabilitation training).
record.buildable: Yes, combining existing haptic feedback devices, force sensors, and AI movement analysis models is feasible.

record.idea: A "Structural Integrity" score for the tortilla during the cooking process. Based on real-time visual analysis (e.g., bubble formation, edge setting), it predicts the likelihood of the tortilla breaking during the flip or cutting, like a wall's stability.
record.gap: Cooks lack real-time objective information on the internal stability of the tortilla to confidently execute critical steps like flipping or cutting without breakage.
record.removed_assumption: Assumes cooks must rely on intuition or experience to judge the tortilla's readiness for handling without breaking.
record.who_has_problem: Cooks who are unsure when their tortilla is structurally stable enough to handle without breaking. "If the pan is too cold or too hot, it can lead to issues like a tough, rubbery tortilla or one that doesn't hold its shape." (https://tortilladepatatas.org/en/guides/classic-tortilla-masterclass/)
record.why_now: Advances in real-time AI vision for cooking processes and predictive analytics from visual cues.
record.buildable: Yes, with a dataset of tortillas at various stages of structural integrity, AI models can be trained to recognize visual cues.

record.idea: A "Tortilla Heritage" app that, after you finish cooking, uses your sensory feedback (sweetness, texture, doneness) to map your tortilla's characteristics onto a historical spectrum of regional tortilla styles, identifying its "lineage".
record.gap: Cooks cannot easily place their homemade tortilla within the diverse historical and regional spectrum of Spanish tortilla styles based on their sensory experience.
record.removed_assumption: Assumes understanding regional tortilla styles is an abstract, expert domain rather than a comparative, experiential one.
record.who_has_problem: Home cooks and enthusiasts who want to understand the cultural context and stylistic characteristics of their tortilla. "Consistency of the tortilla is also a point of debate, with some preferring a firm omelette and others a runnier, 'oozy' one, such as the 'Betanzos' style..." (https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/oct/12/tortilla-town-betanzos-no-onionists-spanish-omelette-recipe-rivalry)
record.why_now: AI capabilities for classifying subjective sensory feedback and the availability of cultural/historical data that can be digitized and structured.
record.buildable: Yes, through collecting and categorizing data on regional tortilla characteristics and training AI models to map sensory inputs to these categories.

record.idea: A "Post-Mortem Analysis" tool for failed tortillas. You upload photos/videos of a tortilla that didn't turn out well, and the AI suggests specific "structural" weaknesses (e.g., undercooked potato core, poor egg distribution) and how to reinforce them next time.
record.gap: Cooks lack a specific, visual-based diagnosis for why their tortilla failed, hindering their ability to learn and improve.
record.removed_assumption: Assumes cooks must guess the reasons for their tortilla failures or consult generic troubleshooting guides.
record.who_has_problem: Home cooks frequently encountering common pitfalls in tortilla preparation who need specific feedback for improvement. (https://tortilladepatatas.org/en/guides/classic-tortilla-masterclass/, https://foodiekake.substack.com/p/tortilla-de-patatas-101-a-guide-to)
record.why_now: Advances in AI vision for defect detection and failure analysis, applied to complex visual patterns in food.
record.buildable: Yes, by compiling a dataset of failed tortillas with known causes and training AI models for visual diagnosis and prescriptive recommendations.

frame_a.name: Traditional Tortilla de Patatas Preparation and Evaluation
frame_a.friction: Achieving specific sensory attributes (texture, doneness, taste) requires precise, often intuitive, control over ingredient quality, ratios, and cooking techniques, which are difficult to quantify and teach. The "physics of the flip" is a critical, manual technique.

slots.materials: Eggs (fresh, specific type), potatoes (floury vs. waxy, specific cut), olive oil (EVOO, low acidity), salt, optional onions.
slots.mechanics: Gentle confiting of potatoes (around 130°C), draining oil, mixing with beaten eggs, resting mixture, pan heating (low-medium), slow setting of egg, the "physics of the flip", achieving specific internal doneness (moist/runny vs. firm).
slots.goals: A perfect tortilla with specific sensory attributes (taste, texture, appearance), balanced ingredients, proper internal doneness, structural integrity (holds shape, but not dry).
slots.emotions: Pride in mastery, frustration with failure, satisfaction from perfect execution, culinary passion, debate/rivalry (e.g., onion vs. no onion, runny vs. firm).
slots.constraints: Limited ingredients, specific temperature control, time sensitivity (potatoes must not burn, eggs not overcooked), pan choice (non-stick), "physics of the flip" skill requirement.
slots.rituals_timing: Resting the potato-egg mixture (10+ minutes), cooking potatoes gently, specific cooking order, quick flipping technique.

slots.materials: Unmortared stones of various shapes and sizes, often local.
slots.mechanics: Selecting stones (fitting shape, size, weight), lifting, placing without mortar, creating a stable interlocking structure, batter (slope) for stability, through-stones, hearting (filling gaps).
slots.goals: A stable, durable, visually pleasing wall, boundary, or structure that withstands weather and time, often without a foundation.
slots.emotions: Patience, satisfaction from creating something lasting, physical exertion, pride in craftsmanship, connection to tradition/landscape.
slots.constraints: Irregular stone shapes, gravity, weather, physical strength, no mortar (reliance on friction and weight distribution), understanding of load-bearing.
slots.rituals_timing: Slow, iterative process; careful selection and placement of each stone; often seasonal work; knowledge passed down through apprenticeship.

friction_points: Tortilla materials are perishable and undergo chemical transformation; dry-stone materials are durable and are physically arranged.
Tortilla mechanics involve precise temperature control and a single, critical fast action; dry-stone mechanics involve slow, iterative placement and structural interlocking.
Tortilla goals are ephemeral and sensory; dry-stone goals are permanent and structural.
Tortilla outcomes are judged immediately; dry-stone outcomes are judged for long-term stability and aesthetics.
Tortilla constraints involve delicate ingredient balance and heat management; dry-stone constraints involve irregular material shapes and reliance on gravity for stability.
Tortilla processes involve specific resting periods and quick, critical techniques; dry-stone processes involve continuous, cumulative placement over extended periods.

personas.who: María, a home cook who has made countless tortillas for her family, but occasionally struggles with the "perfect flip" or inconsistent texture, despite following recipes diligently.
personas.would_do: She would want to understand why her tortillas sometimes fail, in a way that goes beyond "add more egg" or "cook longer," and learn to predict the outcome before it's too late.

personas.who: Javier, a young chef trying to perfect a traditional Spanish menu for his new restaurant, focusing on authentic tortilla de patatas. He needs to consistently produce high-quality tortillas under time pressure, and train new staff to do the same, often without a highly experienced mentor present.
personas.would_do: He would use the collision to standardize the non-standardizable aspects of tortilla making, ensuring consistency and quality across his kitchen staff without losing the "art" of it.

personas.who: Elena, an amateur food blogger and photographer, who wants to document the "science" behind traditional Spanish cooking. She's fascinated by the physics and chemistry of food but finds traditional recipes too vague for her analytical approach.
personas.would_do: She would use the collision to create a visual and data-driven guide that translates intuitive cooking knowledge into observable, repeatable metrics for home cooks and fellow enthusiasts.
